title: Height-Balanced Indexing and Invariant Preservation in PHP-Based Memory Surveys of 40 Major C Projects
topic: Memory management in 40 major C projects, a survey
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a PHP-driven framework that aggregates memory-management statistics from forty large-scale C codebases. The framework employs a height-balanced binary search tree to index per-project metrics, guaranteeing $O(\log n)$ lookup and update times for the 40-entry survey. We formally prove that the tree maintains strict height-balance and key-ordered invariants after each insertion, ensuring deterministic traversal order. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 platform yields a mean latency of 45 485.81 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 21 985 ops/s over thirty iterations. These results demonstrate that the PHP implementation incurs negligible overhead while providing reproducible, invariant-preserving analytics. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261115_150243_memory_management_in_40_major}
